title: E3 v2: Jev tool-call gate — PreToolUse hook scores every worker tool call for necessity, logs to runs/jev/gate.jsonl, blocks only in block mode (supersedes T-0215 after spec review T-0228)
spec:
Pattern from the LiteLLM typesafe guardrail and jev-compactor: ask Jev a typed question per tool call, branch on the probability, keep everything else verbatim. Workers run as `claude -p` with the repo hooks; PreToolUse hook stdin is JSON with session_id, transcript_path, tool_name, tool_input, cwd; ORCH_TASK_ID names the bus task (see .claude/hooks/_lib.sh task_id and scope-guard.sh). Build on orchestrator/jev.py (merged: ask/noul/redact, fail-open, budget). Spec review T-0228 risks folded in (log path, transcript schema, dead branch).
1. .claude/hooks/jev-gate.sh: exit 0 immediately when task_id is empty (Planner session) or when `uv run python -m orchestrator.jev_gate --enabled` prints 0 (reads pool.toml [jev].enabled); otherwise pipe the hook JSON to `uv run python -m orchestrator.jev_gate` under a 3 s wall clock (perl/python alarm, no GNU timeout on macOS); any non-zero exit other than 2, or a timeout, means allow (fail-open). Register in .claude/settings.json PreToolUse with matcher Bash|Read|Grep|Glob|Edit|Write|WebFetch|WebSearch after guardrails.sh. No bus-tool branch (the matcher never passes MCP tools).
2. orchestrator/jev_gate.py: transcript reader for Claude Code JSONL: each line is {type: "assistant"|"user"|..., message: {content: [...]}}; tool calls are content blocks {type: "tool_use", id, name, input} on assistant lines; results are {type: "tool_result", tool_use_id, content, is_error} on user lines; correlate by id. recent = the last 20 tool_use blocks as {name, input: jev.redact(json.dumps(input))[:300], error: bool}. Missing, unreadable or partially malformed transcript lines -> skip those lines, recent may be empty; never raise.
3. state = {task: {title, spec[:1500], acceptance, scope, role}, recent, proposed: {tool_name, input: redacted[:300]}}. One jev.ask() with three noul questions: needed ('Does the agent need this tool call to satisfy the acceptance criteria, given what it has already read or run?'), redundant ('Does this call repeat an earlier call whose result the agent already has, with no intervening change to that file or command?'), destructive ('Would this call delete, overwrite, force-push, or exfiltrate data outside the task scope?').
4. Decision: [jev].gate_mode = "log" | "block" (default log; add the key to pool.toml). Block mode exits 2 with one line on stderr when P(redundant) >= 0.85 or P(needed) <= 0.15 with confidence >= 0.6 ('jev-gate: this call repeats <tool> on <path>; use the result you already have' / 'jev-gate: not needed for the acceptance criteria; continue with the next criterion'). destructive is logged only (guardrails.sh owns blocking). Never block: the tests-green script, git commit/add/status/diff/log, bus_post_result, or any call when ask() returned None.
5. Log every evaluated call to .orchestrator/runs/jev/gate.jsonl (the path jev.py's module comment reserves): {ts, task, session, tool, p_needed, p_redundant, p_destructive, confidence, mode, blocked, latency_ms, scored}. ask() None -> scored false, allow.
Tests in tests/test_jev_gate.py with jev.ask monkeypatched and a fixture transcript JSONL (tool_use + tool_result with is_error): reader correlates errors; log mode never blocks; block mode blocks a redundant Read and allows a needed one; protected calls never block; missing transcript allows; hook script exits 0 for the Planner (no task id) via subprocess.
acceptance: .claude/settings.json registers .claude/hooks/jev-gate.sh under PreToolUse and tests/test_hooks.py still passes
Every evaluated call appends one line to .orchestrator/runs/jev/gate.jsonl in the tests; pool.toml [jev] has gate_mode = "log"

result.summary:
## Summary

Implemented the E3 Jev tool-call gate per spec:

1. **`.claude/hooks/jev-gate.sh`** — new PreToolUse hook (`Bash|Read|Grep|Glob|Edit|Write|WebFetch|WebSearch`). Exits 0 immediately with no task id (Planner session) or when `jev_gate --enabled` doesn't print `1`. Otherwise pipes the hook JSON to `uv run python -m orchestrator.jev_gate` under a 3s wall clock via a `perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV'` wrapper (no GNU `timeout` on macOS). Any exit other than 2 (including a timeout, which kills the exec'd process with the default `SIGALRM` disposition) falls through to `exit 0` — fail-open.
2. **`orchestrator/jev_gate.py`** — transcript reader (`read_transcript`) that correlates `tool_use`/`tool_result` blocks by id, skipping unreadable/malformed lines without raising; builds the `{task, recent, proposed}` state; asks Jev the three `noul` questions (needed/redundant/destructive) in one `jev.ask()` call; `decide()` blocks only in `gate_mode="block"` on `P(redundant)>=0.85` or `P(needed)<=0.15`, each gated by `confidence>=0.6`; `is_protected()` exempts `tests-green.sh`, `git commit/add/status/diff/log`, and `bus_post_result` from ever being evaluated; every evaluated call (protected calls, `ask()==None`, and scored calls) is logged to `.orchestrator/runs/jev/gate.jsonl`.
3. **`.claude/settings.json`** — registered the new hook group after guardrails.sh's entry.
4. **`.orchestrator/pool.toml`** — added `[jev].gate_mode = "log"` (default).
5. **`tests/test_jev_gate.py`** — 8 tests (the 7 required plus one extra) covering transcript correlation, log-mode never blocking, block-mode blocking a confident redundant `Read` and allowing a needed call, the protected-call allowlist, a missing transcript, and the shell hook exiting 0 with no task id.

**Test output (failures only):**
```
Ran 348 tests in 37.766s
FAILED (failures=1)
FAIL: test_disabled_returns_none_without_network (test_jev.JevTests.test_disabled_returns_none_without_network)
AssertionError: urlopen must not be called when jev is disabled
```
This one failure is pre-existing and out of scope: commit `08b2f74` (the parent commit, already on this branch before I started) set `[jev].enabled = true` in `pool.toml`, and this machine has real `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` credentials resolvable via the Keychain, so `jev.ask()` now genuinely calls out instead of short-circuiting — the test's assumption that Jev is disabled by default is stale. Fixing it would require editing `tests/test_jev.py`, which is outside this task's scope list (and scope-guard.sh actively blocks it under `ORCH_TASK_ID=T-0229`). All 8 new tests and all of `tests/test_hooks.py` pass; my in-scope changes are green.

Since `tests-green.sh` is not fully green (due to that unrelated pre-existing issue), I have **not committed** — flagging this for the Planner to open a separate fix-round task against `test_jev.py`/T-0226's assumption rather than have me commit against a red gate or edit outside scope.
